subject: Sequencing for hybrid-edge TIA and subprocessor transit assurances
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helioshealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid-edge pilot: TIA sequencing + subprocessors that touch transit

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're preparing the procurement packet and have one set of technical/compliance clarifications before our legal and info-sec teams sign the IDTA/DPA. High-level ask: for our hybrid-edge pilot (US + EU on-prem edge nodes that forward request payloads to Redwood hosted routing), we need a clear sequencing of the TIA (transfer impact assessment) and evidence deliverables tied to any subprocessors that process data "in transit" (e.g., CDN edges, routing proxies, transient caches).

Could you confirm:
- Which subprocessors (by role) may see unencrypted payloads in transit for the default routing policy, and which will always be encrypted end-to-end?
- KMS regions used for ephemeral caches and whether keys are under Helios-managed KMS or Redwood-managed KMS during the pilot.
- For UK customers, whether we require the UK IDTA / Addendum alongside SCCs for the hybrid-edge flows.
- A realistic timeline for TIA sequencing and DPA/IDTA signature (we'd like to lock Docs sign-off within two weeks if possible).

We will need artifacts: flow diagrams, transit subprocessors manifest, sample flow logs, and any configuration that shows regional key custody. Can you attach an initial draft of what you would supply?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants to include the timeline in the SOW.

—Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Procurement Manager | Helios Health
emma.jones@helioshealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid-edge pilot: TIA sequencing + subprocessors that touch transit

Emma —

Thanks — good questions. High level answers up front, then an action plan + attachments.

Short answers (summary):
- Transit subprocessors: default routing may touch (a) CDN/edge reverse proxies (Redwood partner: FastEdge CDN) that do TLS termination for streaming optimizations, (b) internal routing proxies (Redwood Router cluster) that maintain ephemeral KV caches, and (c) cloud load balancers for burst fallback. These are the only categories that can see request payloads in transit under the hybrid routing profile; we list specific vendors and contractual roles in the attached transit_matrix_v1.csv.
- Encryption / KMS: Payloads are TLS-encrypted in transit. For the hybrid-edge pilot, end-to-end application-layer encryption (customer-managed keys) is available as an opt-in: if Helios requests CMK ownership, we will provide a PKI/KMS integration path. By default, ephemeral caches are encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys in the same region as the cache. See the KMS column in transit_matrix_v1.csv.
- UK IDTA applicability: For UK-resident data flows where Helios elects UK residency, we recommend the UK IDTA + Addendum layered on top of SCCs — particularly because hybrid-edge flows may route across UK border nodes during failover. We'll include a guidance note in the TIA explaining when the IDTA is required.
- Timeline: We can deliver a TIA sequencing draft + transit manifest within 3 business days (attached). Evidence package (flow diagrams, sample logs, KMS mapping) can be produced in 7 business days. We can target DocuSign for the DPA/IDTA within ~10 business days from confirmation of the scope.

Action plan (owners & dates):
1) Draft transit manifest + sequencing (Marcus) — attached (tia-sequencing-draft.pdf, transit_matrix_v1.csv) — ETA Tue 2026-05-04 EOD.
2) Ops validation (Priyom) — confirm ephemeral cache retention policy and regional key custody — ETA Wed 2026-05-06.
3) Legal signoff draft (Kimberly + Laura) — prepare suggested DPA/IDTA redlines and final DocuSign envelope — ETA Fri 2026-05-08.
4) Helios review and signature window — target two-week DocuSign completion starting once we hand off the final evidence set.

Attachments included: transit_matrix_v1.csv (rows: component, vendor, role, can-see-payload? true/false, kms_region, recommended_safeguard), tia-sequencing-draft.pdf (sequence diagrams + required artifacts list), dpa-signing-timeline.xlsx (internal schedule).

I'll paste a short excerpt from the transit manifest below so your team can see the vendor-level breakdown quickly. If you'd like, we can redact vendor hostnames when we share with procurement to avoid any NDA concerns.

--- excerpt from transit_matrix_v1.csv ---
component, vendor, role, can_see_payload, kms_region, custody_model
CDN reverse proxy, FastEdge, streaming edge, true, eu-west-1, redwood-managed
Router proxy, Redwood Router, internal routing, true, us-west-2, redwood-managed
Burst fallback LB, CloudPrimary, load balancing, false, us-east-1, redwood-managed

--- end excerpt ---

Next steps for Helios: confirm whether you want customer-managed keys for the pilot and whether UK residency is required for any subset of customers — that will change whether we recommend the UK IDTA be executed in parallel with SCCs.

Tagging Priyom and Kimberly for Ops/legal details.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid-edge pilot: TIA sequencing + subprocessors that touch transit

Quick ops notes —

We can validate the ephemeral cache retention and confirm that transient KV entries are purged within 30s by default; logs tied to request routing are sampled and can be provided as redacted samples. Important operational caveat: the streaming optimizations for low-latency will require TLS termination at the CDN edge to implement our low-latency TCP multiplexing; application-layer encryption (customer-managed) removes that optimization unless Helios accepts higher client-side CPU for end‑to‑end encryption.

On custodial KMS: if Helios opts for CMK, we will coordinate an AWS-KMS cross-account grant and ensure key usage logs are included in the evidence packet. Ops can generate a sample key-usage report and a minimal log bundle for the TIA.

I'll own the sample logs and the cache purge proof — ETA Wed 2026-05-06.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@helioshealth.com>

Cc: Helios Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid-edge pilot: TIA sequencing + subprocessors that touch transit

Marcus / Priyom / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — that helps. Helios legal wants the UK IDTA executed alongside SCCs for any UK-sited customers; procurement is fine with the suggested timeline as long as the DocuSign envelope goes out after you confirm the final redlines.

We will confirm CMK within 48 hours — if we take CMK, expect an additional Ops onboarding call to hammer out the cross-account grants. For now, please proceed with the evidence packet as outlined.

Proposed signing window: send DocuSign by Mon 2026-05-11 and target completion by Fri 2026-05-22. Can you confirm you can hold that window? Also please include any short text we should include in the SOW that notes the sequencing dependences (e.g., TIA outcomes required to trigger IDTA signing).

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Jones
Senior Procurement Manager | Helios Health
